title: Tokyo's Shinjuku Station Tests Trash Can Robots
paragraphs: Shinjuku Station in Tokyo is Japan's busiest train station, with more than 2.7 million people passing through the wider station area every day. Now, the station is testing robot trash cans that move around by themselves.

The test is being run by the railway company JR East. It began on September 8, 2026, and is planned to continue until late November. Three robot trash cans are being tested. They work on weekdays from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. in an underground area of the station inside the ticket gates.

Each robot is just over one meter tall. The robots move very slowly, at about 20 centimeters per second, and they use sensors to avoid people and stop quickly if needed. They follow set routes around the station, and people can throw away general trash and plastic bottles in them. When a robot is full, it goes back to a collection point by itself.
The robots also have a fun design. They have big googly eyes and are decorated with Shinjukuma, the station's bear mascot.

Why does the station need robot trash cans? At the station, the normal trash cans have to be emptied by hand more than 10 times a day. Also, the number of fixed trash cans has been reduced for reasons of cleanliness and security. JR East hopes that the robots can make the work of cleaning staff easier. The company says the robots are meant to help workers, not replace them.
JR East is also checking whether the robots can move safely through crowds and whether passengers will use them.
So far, many people seem to like them. Some commuters said they were a convenient place to throw away trash, and many tourists have stopped to take photos.
